w: Build fix so the browser compiles. Adds some files the build was missing.
Build fix so V8's WebAssembly interpreter compiles.
Build fix so the browser compiles with Safe Browsing removed. It cuts the download-danger checks, the warning-page hooks and the extension blocklist reporting address.
Stops Autofill from asking Google's servers what the fields in a form are, and from sending form data to them.
n: an opt-in: autofill can ask Google which form fields are which

w: Turns off the Chrome updater's update checks by giving it no update server addresses.
Turns off RLZ, a tool that tells Google which brand and install the browser came from.
Turns off Safe Browsing reports. Nothing is sent to Google about threats, phishing checks or program file checks, and the extended-reporting option is gone.
The browser stops treating Google websites specially. No extra Google tracking headers, no forced SafeSearch and no special cookie handling for Google sites.
Turns off the built-in Google Translate and hides the "Translate to" menu. A custom --translate-script-url switch brings it back.
n: translation comes back as two opt-ins: on-device and Google Translate

w: Stops the RLZ financial ping from reaching clients1.google.com by pointing it at about:blank.
Stops downloading large profile pictures from Google's servers.
Turns off Google Cloud Messaging. The browser never connects to Google to receive push messages.
n: an opt-in: push messages from sites while none of their tabs is open

w: Turns off Domain Reliability, which sends reports about network errors on Google sites to Google.
Blocks every request to a trk: address or a host name ending in qjz9zk. Those mark Google addresses that were scrubbed from the code.
Turns off Gaia, Google's sign-in system. The browser makes no Google account sign-in requests.
Removes links to fonts.googleapis.com. Pages like Reader mode use fonts that come with the browser instead of loading Roboto from Google.
Turns off Chrome Web Store update addresses and pings. On its own it also stops extension update checks; Helium turns those back on.
Build fix. It splits the learn.doubleclick.net text so the build's address replacement does not break the HSTS list generator.
Stops WebRTC debug logs from being saved for upload or uploaded to Google.
Removes Gemini in Chrome (Glic), Screen AI (reads text from images and page layout) and other on-device AI and speech model features.
n: each feature its own opt in (Gemini/Glic, skills, AI permission prompts, page-annotation models, Screen AI)

w: Build fix. Removes tests and data that need prebuilt files, which the source cleanup deletes, and turns off the on-device model service.
Stops the browser from asking Google for the correct time when certificate dates look wrong.
Removes the media autoplay list that ships with Chromium. Autoplay is then decided only from your own browsing.
More build fixes so the browser compiles without Safe Browsing. They simplify the download warning code and the JavaScript optimizer code.
Removes unused Safe Browsing and sign-in fields from the profile's Preferences file.
Blocks background requests: the Google bar, backgrounds and promos on the new tab page, spellcheck dictionary and component update checks, password affiliation lookups and DevTools CSS data.
n: an opt-in that needs a component downloads only that component

w: Removes the Privacy Sandbox attestations list, which Chromium would otherwise ship and load.
Keeps Manifest V2 extensions working. Removes the warnings about them and stops them from being turned off.
Removes the F1 shortcut that opened Google's help page.
Groundwork: moves one JavaScript optimizer setting out of the Safe Browsing settings so it still works without them. Nothing visible on its own.
Removes the source=chrome.ob and source=chrome.rb tracking parameters that were added to searches from the address bar or new tab page.
Includes the hyphenation dictionaries in the browser instead of downloading them later.
Skips the Terms of Service (EULA) screen on first run.
Stops the browser from fetching field trials (Variations), so Google cannot switch experiments on or off in your browser.
Groundwork: adds empty header files where the ungoogled and Bromite chrome://flags entries are registered. Nothing visible on its own.

Changes defaults for privacy. Off: background mode, link pings, preloading, search suggestions, translate offers, autofill, saving passwords and payment checks. Third-party cookies are blocked. The bookmarks bar is shown.
Turns off the Battery Status API. Websites always get a made-up battery state instead of the real one.
Removes the startup bar that warns about missing Google API keys.
Turns off automatic update checks on macOS by setting the check interval to zero. oganesson has no macOS build, so this does nothing in it.
Stops the browser from copying settings and bookmarks from other browsers on first run.
Adds flags that add a little random noise to getClientRects, getBoundingClientRect and canvas measureText results. This makes fingerprinting harder.
Adds a flag to raise the number of connections per host to 15.
Groundwork: adds a small code library that holds the switch names for the fingerprinting flags. Nothing visible on its own.
Turns off the IPv6 connection test to Google DNS. Adds a flag to make that test always fail, so the browser prefers IPv4.
Turns off the intranet redirect detector. It sent DNS lookups for random names when the browser started.
Build fix so the browser compiles with mDNS and local device discovery turned off.
n: an opt-in: one switch for casting and the device discovery it needs

w: Adds a flag to choose what happens with extension files: download them as normal files, or always ask to install.
Adds a flag that stops websites from adding themselves as search engines on their own.
Adds a flag that blocks the "Leave site?" dialog.
Adds a flag to show international domain names in their raw punycode form. This helps you spot look-alike addresses.
Adds a flag to show the profile picture button in the toolbar always, never, or only in Incognito and Guest windows.
Adds a flag that hides the minimize, maximize and close buttons in the browser's own title bar and gives their space to the tabs. A title bar drawn by the system keeps its buttons.
Adds a Suggestions URL field to the search engine edit dialog, so a custom engine can give autocomplete suggestions.
Adds a flag that hides the "Restore pages?" bubble that shows after the browser did not close properly.
Adds a flag to choose whether scrolling the mouse wheel over the tab strip switches tabs.
n: a setting in Settings, also in chrome://flags
t: Scroll the tab strip with the mouse wheel

w: Turns on paste-and-go on all systems. Middle-click the New Tab button to open the link or search from your clipboard.
Adds a flag that hides the bookmarks bar on the New Tab page.
Right-click on the reload button always shows the hard reload and empty cache menu. Before, it only did that with DevTools open.
Adds a flag to limit address bar suggestions to search suggestions. You can add bookmarks and internal chrome:// pages.
Stops Cast/DIAL from sending discovery messages again and again on your local network.
n: part of the casting opt-in: device discovery works normally once casting is on

w: Removes Google-related parts of the interface: Learn more links, Web Store links, synced tabs entries, the Live Caption setting, the update status on the About page, and similar.
Adds a flag that keeps the window open, with a new tab, when you close its last tab.
n: a setting in Settings, also in chrome://flags
t: Close the window with the last tab

w: Adds a flag that opens popup windows as new tabs.
Adds a flag to keep browsing history older than 90 days instead of deleting it.
Turns off Chromium's expanded starter pack of built-in address bar shortcuts (the Site search extras).
Adds a flag that clears all browsing data when the browser closes: history, cookies, cache and passwords.
n: a setting in Settings, also in chrome://flags

w: Adds a flag that asks before closing a window with several tabs, or only before closing the last window.
n: a setting in Settings, also in chrome://flags
t: Ask before closing a window with several tabs

w: Adds a flag to set your own address as the New Tab page.
n: a setting in Settings, also in chrome://flags

w: Adds a flag to turn off tab hover cards or replace them with plain tooltips.
Adds a flag that hides the close button on tabs.
Adds a flag to turn off TLS GREASE values in connections.
Adds a flag to set your own HTTP Accept header on every request.
Adds a flag that stops links and selected text from being dragged.
Adds a flag that hides the extensions menu and the pinned extension icons in the toolbar.
Adds a flag that hides the fullscreen exit X and the "Press F11 to exit" message.
Adds a flag that lets themes apply to Incognito windows.
Adds flags to send no referrer, send no referrer to other sites, or send only the site name as the referrer.
Adds chrome://flags entries for existing switches: disable WebGL, force dark mode, reduced motion, start in Incognito, no pings and the WebRTC IP handling policy.
Adds a flag that shares less system information in headers and JavaScript. For example, sites see two CPU cores.
Adds a flag that stops sending User-Agent Client Hints to websites.
Removes the size limit on proxy auto-config (PAC) files, so big PAC scripts load.

Turns on Certificate Transparency checks, which catch fake HTTPS certificates. Chromium turns them on only in Google Chrome builds. Adds a chrome://flags option "Enforce Certificate Transparency", on by default, so you can turn it off.
Adds a "Spoof WebGL Info" flag. When on, websites see a generic graphics card name and maker instead of your real one. This makes fingerprinting harder.
Adds a flag that gives Incognito and Guest windows the same storage space as normal windows. This makes Incognito harder for sites to detect, but can use a lot of memory.
Adds ungoogled-chromium's license to the chrome://credits page. The "source code available here" link there points to the ungoogled-chromium GitHub page instead of Chromium's.
Always removes the Google AI shortcuts @gemini, @aimode and @page from the address bar and the search engine settings.
Adds about 30 new files from Brave. They read bookmarks, history and extensions from the profiles of other Chromium-based browsers. Nothing visible on its own.

In "Import bookmarks and settings" you can import from Chrome, Chrome Canary, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Yandex, Whale, Arc, Dia and Perplexity Comet. You get bookmarks, history and a new "Extensions" checkbox. Password import is removed for all sources, including Firefox.
Bug fix: site settings set by built-in extensions were forgotten after the first restart. Now they last. No visible change.

Groundwork for Ctrl+Tab switching by most recently used tab. Tabs are ordered by when you last used them, and cycling stops when you release Ctrl, click, or leave the window. A later patch connects it to the keys and the setting.
Adds Zen as a source in "Import bookmarks and settings". It finds Zen (Firefox-based) profiles on Linux (also Flatpak), macOS and Windows, and imports history and bookmarks.
Adds an importer for the Arc browser sidebar. Pinned tabs, top apps and folders (from StorableSidebar.json) become favorites and bookmarks.
Removes the "passwords" and "autofill form data" options from every browser import source, so imports bring only bookmarks, history and similar data.
n: password import comes back if it works with the importers I carry

w: "Import bookmarks and settings" also lists every browser profile it finds in the usual application data folders: Chromium-based ones by their "Local State" file, Firefox-based ones by their profiles.ini. "Choose a profile folder…" adds the profiles in a folder you pick, or up to three levels below it. Firefox profiles with no visits or bookmarks are left out.

Helium's build fix that always builds Safe Browsing's file-type data, even when Safe Browsing is removed. oganesson leaves it out; it builds without Safe Browsing with the Inox and ungoogled-chromium fixes instead.

Groundwork for "Helium services". Adds a Settings > Privacy > "Helium services" page with an on/off switch (on by default in Helium), a field for your own server, and a "services changed" notice. Helium's default server is https://services.helium.imput.net. Later Helium service patches build on it.
n: oganesson's Browser traffic page takes its place, and its settings follow browser traffic; Helium's own server is never used

w: When Helium services change how they work, the app menu button shows a "Services updated" badge and a "Review Helium services updates" item that opens the services settings.
n: the same badge shows instead when certificate data hasn't updated for more than a day, and its item opens Browser traffic

w: Adds a helium:// address scheme that works like chrome://. The address bar, tab hover cards, tab search, status bubble, copied links and suggestions show helium://settings and similar instead of chrome://.
n: shown as oganesson:// here; chrome:// still works

w: Adds a first-run setup page (chrome://setup) that opens at launch until you finish it, and replaces Chromium's own first-run screen. Helium services stay off until you agree there.
n: Helium's first-run setup is never shown

w: Renames the product from "Chromium" to "Helium" everywhere the branding file is used: window titles, About page and installers. Crash reports are also tagged "Helium".
n: renamed to oganesson

w: Makes the browser also look in Google Chrome's native messaging folders (Linux and macOS). Helper programs installed for Chrome, such as password managers, then work with extensions here too.
Brings Google back into the search engine list as a plain engine. It uses a fixed google.com address and none of Chrome's tracking and special parameters, so Google gets no special Chrome treatment.
Changes the default search engine from Google to DuckDuckGo. Every country gets the same list: DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Bing, Google, Qwant, Kagi, Startpage, Brave.
Build switch that includes the built-in search engine logos. Chromium normally has them only in official Chrome builds. Engines show proper icons without downloading them.

Treats everyone as if they were in the EU. The search engine settings show the EU-style list in random order, with the subtitle "This list of search engines is shown in random order", in every country.
Build fix. Removes the search engine description texts that come with the built-in search engine assets and are missing in public sources.

Removes the icon download addresses of the built-in search engines (Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia, Google, Kagi, Qwant, Startpage), so the browser does not fetch their icons. Bundled icons are used instead.
The address bar no longer fetches the search engine site's icon for search suggestions. It shows the bundled icon or the plain search icon.
Adds Kagi reverse image search, so "Search image with Kagi" works when Kagi is your default engine.
Renames the "Brave" search engine to "Brave Search".
Groundwork: adds a hook in the sync engine for a "custom backend" that needs no network or Google sign-in. Nothing visible on its own.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Changes sync so it never uses a Google account. It can run only on a local (roaming-profile) backend or a custom one, otherwise it stays off. Nothing supplies a custom backend, and oganesson drops the patch that would connect one, so Google Sync is gone.
n: Firefox Sync takes its place

w: Groundwork: lists which data types (bookmarks, history, tabs, settings, extensions, themes and more) a custom sync backend may sync. Inactive.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Defines how Helium's encrypted sync data is laid out and checked. New code only; you see nothing.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Adds the encryption used for Helium's encrypted sync data. Groundwork; nothing visible on its own.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Defines what a storage provider must be able to do for Helium's encrypted sync data. Groundwork; nothing visible on its own.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Saves and reads Helium's encrypted sync data. Groundwork; nothing uses it yet.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Lets Chromium's local sync server (the one roaming profiles use) keep its data in memory, not only in a file. Groundwork for Helium's encrypted sync.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Moves the 90-day history expiry into one shared setting. Local behavior does not change. Also lets private sync servers drop history older than 90 days, or trim it when space runs short. Groundwork for Helium's encrypted sync.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Connects Chromium's local sync server (the one roaming profiles use) to Helium's encrypted sync store. Nothing in the patch set ever turns it on. Groundwork.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Adds an extension feature that lets an extension store your encrypted sync data in its own cloud. It is off by default and has no chrome://flags entry, so it does nothing.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Reads the line in an extension's manifest that says it can store sync data. Groundwork; nothing visible on its own.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Browser-side code that talks to a sync-storage extension: requests, setup and time limits. Groundwork; it does nothing yet.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Adds saved settings for private sync: provider, encrypted key and health information. Groundwork.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Reads and writes the private-sync settings and tracks sync errors. Groundwork.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Keeps the sync-storage extension itself, and its data, out of what gets synced. Groundwork for the unused provider sync.
n: inert: Helium's own sync vault, which Firefox Sync replaces

w: Makes the browser always answer "no" to "is this data going to Google?". This turns off features that need Google sync consent, such as web history, Safe Browsing lists, password-account storage and Google Wallet. Also hides Google sign-in device details when private sync is set up.
t: Sync: disable google backed sync integrations

w: Renames the "Appearance" settings page to "Appearance and behavior", with a new icon, and adds a "Behavior" card. The card holds two toggles moved from Appearance: "auto-pin new tab groups" and "split view drag and drop". The light/dark "color scheme mode" menu is removed from Appearance.

Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+C copies the page address. You can switch this off in Settings > Appearance, and then it opens Inspect element. Inspect element moves to Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+E. Web pages can no longer take the DevTools and tab-search shortcuts. On macOS, "Email Link" is gone, "Copy URL" is in the Edit menu and "New split tab" (Cmd+Opt+N) is in the Tab menu.
Two new defaults: tab hover cards no longer show memory use, and the Chrome Web Store icon is hidden.
Adds a "Don't ask again" button to the "make Helium your default browser" bar. Clicking it stops the question for good.

Sends extension installs and updates from the Chrome Web Store through Helium's server, not Google's. Adds the setting "Proxy extension downloads and updates" (on). When it is off, or Helium's services are off, oganesson installs and updates from the Chrome Web Store directly, as Chromium does.
n: without the proxy, Chrome Web Store installs and updates go straight to Google, as in Chromium

w: Turns the browser's extension update checks back on after ungoogled-chromium switched them off, so installed extensions keep updating. Also clears the stock component-update address.

Adds DuckDuckGo-style "!bangs" to the address bar, such as `!w foo` or `!gh foo`. The bang list is downloaded from Helium's server at startup. The setting "Allow downloading the !bangs list" (on) controls this. With it off, bangs only work from saved copies.
n: the !bang list comes only through your own helium-services server; without one, bangs are off

w: Chromium shows the bookmarks bar on every page by default. Helium changes the default to show it only on the new tab page. oganesson keeps Chromium's default.

Downloads spell-check dictionaries from Helium's server instead of Google's. Adds the setting "Allow downloading dictionary files for spell checking" (on). The error message for a failed download names Helium's services.
n: by default oganesson downloads spellcheck dictionaries from Google's server, as Chromium does; through your own server only if you choose it in Browser traffic

w: Turns on Chromium's "HTTPS-First balanced mode" by default (it was off). The browser tries HTTPS first and warns you before using plain HTTP.
Not needed: hover-card images are already on by default outside Mac. ungoogled-chromium's hover-card flag stays.
Helium turns this on by default; oganesson keeps Chromium's default, and the setting stays available.
Helium turns off History Clusters, the groups of related pages in your history, on desktop. oganesson keeps Chromium's default, where they are on.
Helium changes the Chromium project link in the About page so ungoogled-chromium's address replacement does not rewrite it. oganesson leaves this out.

The chrome://credits page names Helium (github.com/imputnet/helium) as the project instead of ungoogled-chromium. Also adds the Svelte license, needed by Helium's welcome page, and a small spacing fix.
Helium switches off Chromium's built-in tips and tutorials for all profiles. oganesson keeps Chromium's behavior.
For a new work or school profile with no domain name, Helium uses the plain single-profile name instead of the enterprise profile name. oganesson keeps Chromium's name.
Helium makes Live Caption always unavailable on desktop. oganesson keeps Chromium's behavior, where it depends on your computer's speech support.
Extension download and update requests always say "Windows x64, Chrome" to the store, whatever your real system is. This hides your platform and gets the standard extension file.
Helium makes the browser's brand list, which sites can read, say "Google Chrome" instead of the browser's own name. oganesson keeps Chromium's behavior.
Adds a separate Helium version number. chrome://version shows a "Helium" row and a "Chromium" row, `--version` prints "Helium X (Chromium Y)", and settings and crash reports use the Helium version.

Helium removes many items from the page right-click menu, such as autofill, Live Caption, Gemini, Lens search, reading mode, Cast, send to your devices, QR code and translate. oganesson keeps Chromium's menu.
Helium removes a safety check in Chrome's tab sync code that failed when you only switched tabs. oganesson leaves it out; it syncs tabs with Firefox Sync.
Helium makes code that waits for a Google push-message ID run right away instead of waiting. oganesson leaves it out.
Groundwork for Helium's own chrome://flags entries. It also hides ChromeOS and Android flags. Nothing visible on its own.
Flag "Maximum frame rate for Energy Saver" (Automatic/30/60/120/Disabled). Default stays at 30 fps throttling.
Flag "Bookmark open-all confirmation". The default keeps the stock "open 15+ bookmarks?" confirmation; the flag lets you turn it off.
Flag "Update channel" (stable or beta, default stable), used for Helium update checks.

Adds the setting "Allow automatic browser updates" (on), or "component updates" on Linux, plus a helper for the update address updates.helium.computer (macOS and Windows only). Also adds an "Update server URL" flag (empty by default). The updater itself is in platform patches.
n: on Windows the Browser updates row in Settings > Browser traffic turns oganesson's own updater's automatic checks on or off (windows/late/updater); on Linux, updates come from the package repository

w: Flag "Middle Click Autoscroll". Off by default on Linux/macOS, on by default on Windows as in stock Chromium.
Helium hides a long list of chrome://flags entries it thinks are broken or useless for Helium. oganesson keeps them visible.
Helium turns off Chromium's "your browser is out of date" check. oganesson keeps Chromium's default.

Removes buttons from "Customize toolbar" that cannot work or are not wanted: Reading mode, Reading list, Tabs from other devices, Google Lens, Search companion, Password manager, Payment methods and Addresses.
n: the Password manager button stays available

w: Lets built-in extensions load their translations from the browser. Groundwork for the built-in uBlock Origin; nothing visible on its own.
Lets built-in extensions read their admin-settings layout from the browser. Groundwork for uBlock Origin's admin settings; nothing visible on its own.
Loads OS and company policy files earlier at startup, so managed extension settings are ready before startup pages load. Nothing visible.
Adds uBlock Origin 1.66.4 source code and the build rules that package it. Build groundwork; nothing visible on its own.
Builds uBlock Origin into the browser as an extension that is always installed.

Makes the built-in uBlock Origin act like a normal extension: you can see and turn it off, and site-access rules apply. It is pinned to the toolbar and allowed in incognito by default. Also lets built-in extensions get past company install blocks.
Sends uBlock's filter-list downloads through Helium's server. Adds the setting "Allow downloading filter lists for uBlock Origin" (on). If it is off, uBlock only uses its bundled lists.
n: by default uBlock Origin updates its filter lists from its own sources; through your own server only if you choose it in Browser traffic

w: Gives uBlock Origin a DNS lookup tool, so it can block trackers that hide behind a site's own subdomain, as in Firefox. It follows your Secure DNS and proxy settings.
n: oganesson uses Helium's patch; tennessine has its own, as it carries no Helium code

w: Helium removes the action suggestions in the address bar, such as manage passwords, update card, run safety check, translate and Google Docs shortcuts. oganesson keeps Chromium's suggestions.

Helium turns on ungoogled-chromium's flag that gives Incognito and Guest the same storage limit as normal profiles, which makes Incognito harder for sites to detect. oganesson keeps the default (off) and the flag stays available.

Core of "Helium Noise", which makes it harder to track you by your device's fingerprint. Each profile gets a secret per-site number, renewed when you clear browsing data. Adds a global setting, a per-site allow/block setting and a flag to disable it. Helium turns it on by default; oganesson ships it off. The per-site page-info panel is dropped.
n: the switch is in Settings > Privacy

w: Adds tiny, site-stable changes to canvas images that pages read back, so sites cannot fingerprint you with them. Helium has it on by default, oganesson off. Has a flag to disable it.
Adds a tiny change (about ±0.01%) to Web Audio sound, so sites cannot fingerprint you with it. Helium has it on by default, oganesson off. Has a flag.
Pages that ask how many CPU cores you have get a believable fake number (even, 2 to 16) that stays the same for each site. Helium has it on by default, oganesson off. Has a flag.
Flag "Disable Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)", for networks that block ECH. Off by default, so ECH stays on.

Adds a "Global Privacy Control" setting for each profile (off by default). When on, sites are told you do not want your data sold or shared. The toggle itself is in the network and security settings patch.
Flag "Use only QUIC v2 for HTTP/3", for networks that block QUIC v1. Off by default.

Flag "Random TLS ClientHello splitting" (changes BoringSSL). It splits the start of a secure connection so the site name is cut in pieces, which can get around some censorship that filters by domain. Off by default.

Changes the Secure DNS provider list in settings. Adds Cloudflare Family and Security, shows NextDNS everywhere, and hides OpenDNS, CleanBrowsing Family and DNS4EU. Google is renamed "Google (8.8.8.8)". Plain Cloudflare and NextDNS addresses are used, and the list is no longer shuffled. The DNS test uses example.com, not google.com.
Flag "Ignore system proxy" (always connect directly). Off by default.
t: Network: ignore system proxy server flag

w: Turns on "Reduce Accept-Language" by default (it was off). Sites get fewer details about your languages, which makes you harder to fingerprint.
Turns off Google's Privacy Sandbox ad features: Topics, and the Protected Audience (FLEDGE) ad-interest feature.
Helium turns this on by default; oganesson keeps Chromium's default, and the setting stays available.
Always uses the normal desktop layout for the toolbar and tabs, whether or not you have a touchscreen.

Adds the setting "Open new tabs next to the active tab" (Appearance, off by default). When on, a new tab opens next to the current tab, or at the end of its tab group, not at the end of the tab strip.
Turns off Chromium's update pop-up for small (non-milestone) updates.
Never shows the "sign in with" account bubble that sites can open through FedCM.
Changes the WebRTC address setting from "default" to "default public interface only", so sites cannot see your local network addresses.
Right-clicking the window title bar shows a "Customize Chrome" item that opens the customization side panel (not in incognito).
Removes the footer from the new tab page (enabled→disabled).
Adds the setting "Cycle through tabs in most recently used order with Ctrl+Tab" (Appearance, off by default).

Blocks Google's component-update server (update.googleapis.com). Component updates come from Helium's server instead, only if its services, your consent and the update setting allow it. Only the certificate revocation list and Widevine (DRM) may register; other components are refused. chrome://components explains the errors when services are off.
n: components come straight from Google's update server by default, or through your own server, never Helium's; the Chrome Root Store and the CT log list may register too, and update checks send no pings

w: Adds an empty built-in extension called "extstore-fixups". Groundwork for the Web Store fixes; nothing visible on its own.
n: works only for what you send through your own helium-services server in Settings > Browser traffic; Helium's own server is never used

w: Adds scripts to chromewebstore.google.com that remove the "Switch to Chrome" banners and pop-ups, stop the store from checking whether you use Chrome, and rename "Add to Chrome" to "Add to Helium".
Adds "Hibernate" and "Hibernate other tabs" to the tab right-click menu. They unload background tabs to free memory.
Turns off the sliding animation when the side panel opens, on all platforms (it was already off on macOS).
Lets you use your own image file as a profile picture (saved as "Custom Avatar Picture.png"). The picker is in a separate Helium settings patch.
Adds "Close tabs to the left" to the tab context menu ("Close tabs above" with vertical tabs).

Lets you change browser keyboard shortcuts (on by default). Adds a list of commands with labels, saves your choices, and supports the macOS menus. The settings page and window wiring are in separate Helium patches.
Adds "Copy URL" / "Copy URLs" to the tab right-click menu. It copies the address of one or all selected tabs, one per line, with chrome:// shown as helium://.
Adds "Mute tab(s)" / "Unmute tab(s)" to the tab right-click menu, working on all selected tabs.

Simplifies the page right-click menu. Back and Forward show only when they work, "Search Google for '<long text>'" becomes "Search with <engine>", the selected-text preview shrinks from 50 to 24 characters, and "Copy link address" moves.
Removes the "make Helium your PDF viewer" bar and the "launch on startup" bar.
Turns on Chromium's built-in screenshot tool in the share menu (it was off). Files are saved as helium_screenshot_*.png.
Turns on Chromium's newer look (all were off): the refreshed toolbar (without the back/forward part), new tab-group colors, the 2026 settings-page refresh and rounded icons.
Adds "Force paste" to the page right-click menu and as a browser command. It types the clipboard text into the selected field, even on sites that block pasting.
Shift+right-click always shows the browser's own menu, even on sites that replace or block right-click. A setting in Appearance, on by default.

Crash reports are never uploaded without consent: consent is forced off when the crash reporter starts, and automatic upload by release channel is off. Reports keep only the names of command-line switches and feature settings, not their values.

Adds a crash-reporting mode (Disabled, Ask or Automatic; default "Ask"; same for all profiles) and report deletion. Official builds upload to crash.helium.computer, which the `--custom-crash-server-url` switch can change. A policy can turn it off. The crash dialog is in another patch.
n: reports would go to Helium's server

w: Removes Google AI pages and resources from the build: Gemini in Chrome, Lens overlay and side panel, "Help me write", contextual tasks, the AI agent, the AI overlay and skills.
n: AI features that come back as opt-ins bring back what they need

w: Turns off the new web-based address-bar dropdown, including its AI mode, so the classic dropdown is used. Also removes the experimental web-based toolbar and browser pages, and swaps one PNG icon for a vector icon.
Build settings for Helium's own remote build servers (NativeLink), which oganesson doesn't use.

Helium turns off four web sign-in features by default: Email Verification, Digital Credentials, creating Digital Credentials and WebOTP (one-time codes from text messages). oganesson keeps Chromium's defaults.
The build uses your system Python 3 instead of the one bundled with Chromium. Build only.
When you restore a session or reopen a closed window, background tabs stay unloaded and show only their saved icon until you click them. Only the selected tab loads right away.
Helium turns this on by default; oganesson keeps Chromium's default, and the setting stays available.
Keeps Google sign-in, session cookies and security-key enrollment working under ungoogled-chromium's domain replacement, which would otherwise rewrite Google's and YouTube's addresses.
Helium turns off the password manager as insecure. oganesson keeps it: malware running as you can read passwords from memory whatever the storage, so a separate manager adds little.
Replaces the shield icon for Security/Privacy with a keyhole shield. In the settings sidebar, the Chrome logo next to "About" becomes a plain info icon.
Moves the "search suggestions" toggle to the Search engine page. Also removes the "Sync and Google services" row and the sync setup pages from profile settings.
n: the Firefox Sync row takes its place

w: Removes the whole "Autofill and passwords" section from settings: payments, addresses, ID documents, travel, shopping, Gemini suggestions and passkeys.
n: oganesson brings the Autofill and passwords section back

w: On the profile ("You and Google") page, removes the Google sign-in promo, the Google account row, "Google services", "Manage your Google Account", the "Profile name and picture" row and the "sync unavailable" message.
Renames labels: the History page's menu item says "History", and the "You and Google" page uses the profile menu's name ("Profiles"/"Profile").
Removes the Safety Hub ("Safety check") page from Privacy settings. Also removes the Safety Hub suggestion on the Notifications page.
When a search in settings finds nothing, the extra help line that links to Google help is no longer shown.
On the About page, removes the two "Learn more" links to Google support pages, the click action on the product logo, and the product subtitle line.
Hides the Google Translate section of Language settings: the offer to translate and the always/never translate lists. Also hides the "translate target" label next to languages.
n: comes back with the translation opt-ins

w: Removes the Safety Hub header and buttons from the Site settings and Notifications pages, and the Safety Hub entry from the Privacy page.
Shows the update status message and icon on the About page again (not on ChromeOS). An earlier patch had hidden them.
Hides the "Third-party cookies" row on the Privacy page. Searching for cookies points to Site settings instead, whose description now mentions cookies and pop-ups.
Removes the Live Caption control from Accessibility settings on Windows and macOS, and the leftover divider lines above "Captions".
Rewrites the help text above the third-party cookie exceptions list. It now just explains the "[*.]" wildcard, without the tracking-protection wording.

Renames the search suggestion toggle to "Suggestions from the search engine". Its text now says that what you type in the address bar is sent to your default search engine, and that this is off in Incognito.
On Linux, shows the "Reset to default theme" label, which stock Chromium hides there. Shortens the label for pinning new tab groups to the bookmarks bar.
Settings now opens on "Appearance and behavior" instead of the profile page. That item moves near the top of the sidebar, and the "AI" item is removed.
Adds an "Add" button to the search engine list. It opens a dialog where "Add as default" adds the engine and makes it the default in one step. Stock Chromium only lets you add site-search shortcuts.
Lets you pick your own PNG or JPEG image (up to 30 MB) as your profile picture. It is cropped to a square and you can remove it later. Clear errors show for files that are too big or can't be read.

Adds a "Keyboard shortcuts" page under System settings. You can search commands, add, remove or change shortcuts, see conflict warnings, and reset everything. It shows only when the `CustomizableBrowserShortcuts` feature is on, which is the default.
The "Delete browsing data" dialog lists all data types from the start instead of hiding them. The "Manage other Google data" row is removed.
Adds a "Crash reporting" setting: Disabled, Ask after a crash, or Send automatically. Disabled deletes waiting reports. Reports would go to Helium's crash server, so it is off in oganesson.
Adds a "Fingerprinting protection" page under Privacy. It has an on/off switch for Helium's noise feature, an explanation, and lists of per-site exceptions. The protection is on by default.

Renames "Security" to "Network and security" and splits it into Network, Privacy signals and Security sections. Adds a "Global Privacy Control" switch and moves "Do Not Track" next to it, without its confirmation dialog. Removes the old Do Not Track and "universal opt-out" switches from the cookies page.
Part of Helium's own sync setup. oganesson leaves it out because it uses Firefox Sync instead.
Makes the browser frame more compact. The address bar and toolbar buttons go from 34 to 28 px tall, tabs from 35 to 31 px, and address bar items get less rounded corners (radius 12 to 6).

Makes buttons, menus and dialogs less rounded. Buttons are rounded rectangles (7 px) instead of pills, and menus and dialogs have 8 px corners. Buttons on internal pages have 8 px corners and never wrap their text.

Restyles the shared look of internal chrome:// pages (Settings, History, Downloads, Extensions and more). Removes the Chrome logo from headers. Round buttons and pill-shaped search boxes become rounded squares, card shadows become thin outlines, and toasts and menu items get more compact.
The new tab page is always the browser's own page, whatever the default search engine is. Stock Chromium gives that page only to Google users and loads the search engine's own page otherwise.

Strips the new tab page down to centered shortcut tiles and an icon-only Customize button. Removed: the Google bar and logo, the search box and AI box, voice search, Lens upload, cards, promos, the wallpaper search button, and background credit and undo messages.

Removes the curved corners where the toolbar meets the tab strip and around the page area, so edges are flat. In vertical tabs it also removes the strip's outline, shadow and see-through blur when it expands on hover.

Makes the address bar a rounded rectangle instead of a pill, with tighter spacing. Permanently hides several icons: AI Mode, Lens, offers and rewards, cookie controls, payments, and autofill sign-in and card info. chrome://, extension and file:// pages no longer show a text label next to the site icon.
Address bar action icons (translate, bookmark star and so on) are always plain icons, with no text label or colored chip. The "Open in app" chip is replaced by a plain app icon.

Several tab strip changes:
- Each tab is a separate rounded box, and tabs are narrower (190 px instead of 232).
- The close "x" shows only when the mouse is over a tab.
- The sound icon sits next to the site icon, left of the title, and no longer fades.
- Tab group headers and underlines are restyled.
- Clicking a tab's sound icon to mute it is on by default.

Tabs no longer show a spinning ring around the site icon. Sleeping tabs, and restored tabs that have not loaded yet, show a faded gray icon instead of Chrome's dotted ring. Chrome's tip popup about sleeping tabs is removed. The Performance setting is renamed "Differentiate hibernated tabs".
When you go to another page on the same site, the tab keeps the old site icon until the new one loads, instead of flashing a blank globe. It also detects pages with no icon more reliably.
The "+" new tab button and other tab strip buttons are rounded squares (8 px corners) instead of circles.
Toolbar buttons and their hover highlights are rounded squares instead of circles. The split-view button shows only if you pinned it, not whenever the tab is in a split.
Removes the thin vertical dividers in the toolbar: the one before the extensions puzzle icon and the one in the pinned actions area.
You can drag the window by any empty space in the toolbar, like a title bar. Stock Chromium allows this only with vertical tabs. Also adds a macOS fix for a crash while a window is closing.

In Customize Chrome > Toolbar, you can hide the Back, Reload, profile, Extensions, main Menu and Media controls buttons. All are shown by default, so nothing changes until you hide one. The settings list is also reordered, and menus still open from the top corner when the menu button is hidden.

Moves the Tab Search button (list of open tabs) from the tab strip to the toolbar, with a new icon. You can pin it in Customize Toolbar. If it isn't pinned, it shows only while the tab search popup is open and goes away 2 seconds after it closes. Removes the old tab strip button and the vertical strip's tab search button.

Makes the address bar suggestion list more compact. Rows shrink from 40 px to 28 px, corners become 12 px with a smaller shadow, and the highlighted row is a rounded box. Special icon backgrounds on action suggestions are removed, and suggestion chips are restyled.
In the three-dot menu, the round buttons (like the zoom +/- row) get 8 px rounded-square highlights. The tinted backgrounds behind the profile, "Update" and "Set as default browser" rows are removed.

Reorganizes the three-dot menu. Removed: the profile submenu, "Passwords and autofill", "Send to your devices", Translate, "Reading mode", the vertical tabs switch, the Safety Hub row and Reading List. "Bookmarks and lists" becomes "Bookmarks". "Extensions" opens the extensions page directly. "Customize Chrome" moves to the main menu and "Exit" into More tools. The Update item moves from the top to the normal notice area.
n: "Passwords and autofill" stays in the menu; Translate returns with the translation opt-in

w: The three-dot toolbar button always looks like a plain toolbar button. Chrome's colored pill with text such as "Update" is gone. The button now draws its border.
Removes the "Reading list" submenu from the Bookmarks submenu of the three-dot menu.
In split view, removes the small floating toolbar at the bottom-right of the inactive pane. The pane outline and screen-capture border are drawn as plain rounded rectangles.

Right-clicking the divider between split-view panes opens the split-view menu (swap, close one side, exit split, change direction). The divider handle is thinner (2 px instead of 4 px). "Send feedback" is removed from that menu. "Close left/right tab" is fixed for right-to-left languages. The split-view promo text color is softer.
Groundwork only; nothing visible on its own. Adds helper code for Helium's window corner sizes, which later patches use.

Restyles split view. The gap around panes shrinks from 8 px to 3 px and the inner padding from 4 px to 2 px. Pane corners use Helium's corner sizes, and the bottom outer corners match the window's rounded corners (except in fullscreen or while a drop target is shown).

Adds the setting "Show a rounded frame around web contents" under Settings > Appearance, on by default. A single page then sits inside a small inset, rounded, outlined frame, like split view. It is off in fullscreen and in non-normal windows. Also fixes the reported page size so it excludes the border.

Makes the rounded page frame meet an open side panel cleanly. On the side where a panel is attached, the page drops its inset and outer rounding and draws a separator. Removes the small curved corner piece where the toolbar separator meets the panel.

Restyles the "drop here to split" area that appears when you drag a link or tab to the page edge. It has tighter padding, an outline, neutral icon and text colors, and a faster animation (450 ms to 300 ms). It also appears sooner (delay 1000 ms to 500 ms) and works with the rounded frame and an open side panel.
The Customize side panel stops reacting to which kind of tab is active. It no longer jumps back to the overview page or changes its sections when you switch between the new tab page and other tabs.

Restyles the side panel. Margins shrink from 8 px to 3 px on most sides, the header is shorter (40 px to 32 px), and the resize handle is thinner. Corners match the window. The minimum width is 200 px, and dragging snaps to the default width. Chrome's drop shadow around the panel is off.

Removes buttons for unused features from the list of actions you can pin to the toolbar or side panel: Reading list, Tabs from other devices, shopping and price insights, Google Lens, Send tab to self, Translate, Addresses, Payment methods and Passwords. Translate, password and card icons are also removed from installed web app title bars. These are mostly Google features or ones disabled by other patches.
n: the Password manager button stays available

w: Hides the "Autofill settings" and "Manage your Google Account" buttons in the profile menu.
The "extension installed" popup no longer shows the extra tips text: how to use it, its keyboard shortcut link and where to manage it. Only the title and icon remain.

If an extension download is blocked because Helium services or extension downloads are off, the downloads bubble says "Extension downloads are disabled" instead of "Blocked by your organization". It also has a button that opens chrome://settings/privacy/services.
n: works only for what you send through your own helium-services server in Settings > Browser traffic; Helium's own server is never used

w: When you switch the address bar to a search engine with Tab, the chip shows just the engine name (for example "DuckDuckGo") instead of "Search DuckDuckGo". Spacing is tighter.
Bookmarks bar buttons and folders get a 6 px rounded-rectangle hover highlight instead of a round pill.
Restyles new tab page shortcut tiles. Icons sit in rounded squares instead of circles, tile corners are 10 px instead of 4 px, and site icons are larger (30 px) and sharp.

Tightens the look of all web-based side panels (bookmarks, history, customize and so on). Corners are smaller (12 px to 9 px), gaps between cards are smaller, headings are shorter, and the hidden back button no longer takes space. Search fields are rounded.

Simplifies the Customize side panel. Removed: the theme preview, the image and "managed by" rows, the toolbar illustration, category titles, intro text and the reorder tip. Theme editing becomes a "Change wallpaper" button that goes straight to uploading your own image. "Reset to classic Chrome" becomes "Reset to default".
Replaces the Chrome logo on internal pages (for example the "About" entry in Settings) with Helium's star-shaped logo.
Letter tiles shown for sites with no icon (on new tab shortcuts and similar places) are rounded squares with 14 px corners instead of circles.
New profiles start with the gray theme. "Reset to default" also returns to gray, and the stock blue "Default" swatch is removed from the theme color picker.

Redesigns small pop-up messages (toasts, such as "Link copied"). They are smaller (32 px instead of 48 px), have 8 px corners and a thin outline but no shadow, use the address bar color, and appear at the right under the toolbar instead of centered. They scale in instead of sliding down.
Buttons on security warning pages (for example "Your connection is not private") have 8 px corners instead of pill shapes, and slightly less padding.
When there is no saved window position, the first browser window opens in the center of the screen, not near the top-left corner.

Removes several items from Developer Tools: the Recorder's "Send feedback" link, the "What's New" panel, the Gemini promo popup, the Help submenu, and the Google account sync and Google Developer Program section in DevTools settings.

Removes Chrome's first-run intro and feature showcase pages, the intro sounds, and promo images (Password Manager family sharing, Gemini, Google Drive sign-in). Most people won't notice, because Helium shows its own onboarding.
Makes the bookmarks bar tighter: separators are thinner (1 px instead of 2 px) with less space around them, and the end margins are smaller.
On the "Who's using Helium?" profile picker, removes the decorative side banner images and the hidden action when you click the logo. Footer controls are spaced evenly.
The tab-group edit bubble no longer shows the "learn more about saved groups" footer, which stock Chromium shows up to 5 times.
Removes the illustration at the top of the new-profile customization dialog and makes the header shorter (130px instead of 170px).

The settings and menus for Helium's built-in bangs (search shortcuts such as !w). oganesson leaves it out: bangs work only through your own helium-services server, and Settings > Browser traffic updates their list.

Infobars (bars under the toolbar, such as "Restore pages?") are shorter (44 px instead of 56 px) and use the toolbar color. Their drop shadow is replaced by thin side separators that fit the rounded page frame and vertical tab layout.
Text buttons across the browser are 2 px shorter.
Installed web apps get a tighter title bar toolbar with smaller margins. The page title is no longer shown next to the address in the app's top bar.

Changes the built-in colors. In light mode the window frame matches the toolbar, even when the window is inactive. The address bar is slightly see-through. Background tabs are transparent with a faint highlight on hover. The selected tab uses the address bar color, and separators and bubble borders are toned down in dark mode. On Linux, system theme tab colors change to match. Custom themes are not affected.

The tab strip area paints the window frame or theme background itself. In fullscreen, the area behind the tabs shows the theme image instead of a plain color, so themes look consistent behind the tabs.

The link preview bubble in the bottom-left corner (it shows the address when you hover a link) becomes a floating rounded pill with 16 px corners, a soft shadow and a thin outline. It sits 8 px from the window corner and uses address bar colors.

The Incognito and Guest new tab pages lose their "Learn more" links to Google help pages. The Incognito page also loses the third-party cookie blocking box, and its text is rewritten without mentioning Google.
Turns on overlay scrollbars on Windows and Linux too (stock Chromium has them only on Mac and ChromeOS). Page scrollbars follow the system setting, so they can be thin and hide when not in use.

Replaces Chromium's Google-blue colors with Helium's indigo blue (#3450d1) and slightly different grays, in the browser UI, internal pages (Settings, chrome://flags and so on) and the theme picker's gray swatch.

Restyles chrome://flags with a rounded search box and dropdowns, an outline focus ring, and full flag descriptions in narrow windows. The "Default" choice shows its real state, such as "Default (Enabled)", with a * and a footnote if the command line or an experiment changed it.
The built-in uBlock Origin, normally hidden, now shows on chrome://extensions with a blue "Helium component" badge, so you can see and manage it. Other extensions can see it but can't uninstall it.
Adds license entries for Helium itself (GPL-3.0), the Instrument Sans font and Tabler Icons to the chrome://credits page. Licensing only.
Helium removes the footer of the password autofill drop-down on login forms ("Manage passwords" and passkey entries). oganesson keeps the password manager, so it keeps this footer and its link.
n: the password manager is kept, so its link stays

w: macOS only: moves the red/yellow/green window buttons closer to the window corner (10 px) and adjusts the space reserved for them and the corner size on macOS 26. oganesson has no macOS build, so this does nothing in it.

The Find-in-page (Ctrl+F) box sits at the top-right of the page instead of hanging under the address bar. It has tighter padding and a smaller shadow, and the magnifier icon is not shown in the address bar while it is open.

Makes Helium's customizable keyboard shortcuts work in browser windows. Your shortcuts replace the built-in ones and apply as soon as you change them. On Mac, the menu bar shortcuts update too. The editor is a separate settings page.

After a crash restart, asks "Would you like to send a crash report?" with "Send report", "No thanks" and "Don't ask again". Unsent reports are deleted. Sent reports go to Helium's crash server. Off in oganesson, along with crash reporting.

The chrome://crashes page follows Helium's crash reporting setting (automatic, ask or disabled) instead of Google's metrics consent. It always lists local crashes and shows the Helium version. Its "Create an issue with details" link opens a GitHub issue instead of the Chromium bug tracker.
n: its issue link points at oganesson

w: Groundwork for Helium's layouts. One setting replaces the on/off vertical tabs switch and holds one of four layouts: Classic (default), Compact, Vertical or Dynamic. Adds a setting for vertical tabs on the right (off by default). Side effects: vertical tabs "expand on hover" is forced off, the "try vertical tabs" popup is removed, and the vertical strip's collapsed state and width are not saved per window.

On the Appearance page, the "Tab strip position" dropdown is replaced by "Browser layout" (Classic, Dynamic, Compact, Vertical). "Show vertical tabs on right side" appears when Vertical is chosen. Several stock options are removed: expand vertical tabs on hover, organizer panel button, "everything menu" button, auto-show tab scroll buttons and "Show tab search button".

Right-clicking the window title bar shows a "Browser layout" submenu (Classic, Dynamic, Compact, Vertical), plus "Tabs on right side" in Vertical. Not shown in Incognito windows. The stock title bar items for vertical tabs, "Send feedback" and tab scroll buttons are removed.

In Vertical layout, Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) collapses or expands the vertical tab strip instead of saving the page. A setting on the behavior page turns this on or off. In other layouts Ctrl+S still saves. Also removes Chromium's Ctrl+Shift+L shortcut for collapsing vertical tabs, and on Mac the Cmd+Alt+N shortcut for a new split tab.
n: Ctrl+S always saves the page here: the setting is off by default. Collapsing vertical tabs uses Firefox's Ctrl+Alt+Z, if free

w: Optional "Centered address bar" setting (off by default). When on, the address bar is narrower (at most 700 px) and centered in the window. The setting is hidden in Compact layout.
Changes the empty space at the end of the tab strip used for dragging the window: 27 px in Classic layout (stock is 42 px) and none in the other layouts.
In Dynamic and Vertical layouts, hides the "+" new tab button (and the divider after the last tab) in the horizontal tab strip. Classic and Compact keep it.

In every layout except Classic, the toolbar is the top row of the window, next to the window buttons. In Compact, the address bar is a fixed 350 px wide. Back and Reload never shrink or move into the overflow menu.
Optional "Minimal URL in the address bar" setting (off by default). When on and not focused, the address bar shows only the site's domain, centered. Clicking it shows the full address.
Adds the Dynamic layout: the toolbar is on top, the tab strip is below it, and the tab strip is hidden while the window has only one tab. Also adjusts frame drawing for this layout on Linux.
Adds the Compact layout: tabs move into the toolbar row, to the right of the address bar, making one combined bar. The "+" button is hidden when it doesn't fit, and the address bar is not centered.

Restyles vertical tabs for the Vertical layout. The strip can be on the right. The button row at the top and the floating rounded corners are removed. The bottom button becomes a labeled "New tab" button. The strip is narrower: 200 px instead of 240, collapsed 42 instead of 56, minimum 160 instead of 126. Resizing snaps to the default width and the collapse animation is shorter. Sound icons sit next to the site icon, and muting by clicking is off while collapsed. "Show tabs vertically/horizontally" is removed from the tab menu.

Improves the toolbar in narrow windows. The extensions (puzzle) button can move into the "..." overflow menu, which no longer has separators. The split tabs button moves there sooner. In Compact, toolbar buttons keep their size and tabs shrink first. When the puzzle button is hidden, extension popups open from the overflow button.

Adds two toolbar buttons, on by default and hideable in Customize Toolbar. In Vertical layout, a sidebar-icon button collapses or expands the vertical tabs. In Dynamic layout, a "+" new tab button appears in the toolbar, replacing the one hidden in the tab strip. Both can move into the overflow menu.

Groundwork for "Frameless mode" (zen mode). Adds Appearance settings: "Automatically hide browser UI until you hover the window edge", plus "Always show the sidebar" (Vertical only) and "Always show the top bar", all off by default. Adds a Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L shortcut to pin the top bar (disabled here) and a "New tab opened" toast. Renames the accessibility toast setting to "Background action confirmation toasts". The hiding itself is a separate patch.
Lets Frameless mode fade out and disable the close, minimize and maximize buttons on Mac, Linux and Windows while the browser UI is hidden.

Adds Zen mode: the toolbar, tab strip and vertical tab sidebar hide and slide back in when the mouse reaches the top or side edge of the window. They stay visible while the address bar is focused or a menu is open, and hide when the window loses focus. The top bar and sidebar can each be pinned. Ctrl+S shows or hides the side tabs, and a toast says "new tab created" when a link opens a tab you can't see. Also fixes pinned tabs per row in the vertical strip.
The browser window can be narrower: 400 px instead of 500 px. The minimum is the same in every layout, so vertical tabs and side panels may overlap at very small widths.
The "Create QR code" dialog makes plain square QR codes with no Chrome dinosaur in the middle, instead of round dots, rounded corners and the dino. Without the logo, the code can also be smaller.

Makes the built-in PDF viewer more compact: the toolbar is 36 px tall instead of 56 px, with smaller text. The sidebar is narrower, and the selected page thumbnail gets a thin outline instead of a thick glow. Removes the "Save to Google Drive" button.
Hides the Live Caption button in the picture-in-picture video window, and its captions panel can never open.
Turns off the circular ripple animation when you click buttons in the toolbar, menus and internal pages such as Settings. Clicks show no ripple, like Chrome on Mac.
Fixes thin visible lines or gaps between parts of the browser window on screens with fractional scaling (such as 125% or 150%). Smoothing is now used only on rounded shapes, not on plain rectangles.
Windows only: fixes where the top of the window sits above the tab strip, so the tabs and toolbar are placed correctly.

macOS only: an optional see-through browser frame (tab strip, toolbar, sidebar, infobars) with the system's frosted-glass blur, tinted by the theme color. Turn on the flag "Native frame materials" in chrome://flags (off by default). Then a "Use native frame materials (experimental)" switch appears in Settings > Appearance, also off by default. oganesson has no macOS build, so this does nothing in it.

When a page is zoomed, the address bar shows the zoom level as text (for example "125%") instead of Chrome's magnifier icon. Clicking it resets zoom to 100%. The zoom popup no longer opens by itself. A "Show the zoom indicator in the address bar" switch in Settings > Appearance is on by default.
Adds 133% and 140% to the zoom steps you go through with Ctrl+plus and Ctrl+minus, between 125% and 150%.

Helium adds a link to the fingerprint noise settings in the page-info panel (opened from the address bar), plus a reload prompt after you change it. oganesson leaves that out. The noise feature and its settings page stay, off by default.

On the History page, "Tabs from other devices" now lists synced tabs when tab sync is on even if you are not signed in to a Google account. This supports sync services that are not tied to a Google account. Sign-in and sync prompts are hidden once tab sync is on.
t: Synced tabs without a Google account

w: When an extension starts debugging the browser, a small bug icon with "Debugging started" appears at the left of the address bar, instead of Chrome's full-width yellow bar. Clicking it lists the extensions, each with a "Stop" button. The yellow bar is still used when no address bar is visible.

Shows page-loading progress as a thin glowing line along the bottom of the address bar, in the theme's accent color. A "Show loading progress in the address bar" switch in Settings > Appearance is on by default.

Restyles the "Press Esc to exit full screen" message: rounded corners, no shadow, dark grey background and smaller text. It stays for 2.5 seconds instead of 3.8 and fades faster. The background is always solid, whatever Chrome's transparency setting says.

Adds a flag "Hide all page actions" in chrome://flags, off by default. When it is on, every icon at the right end of the address bar is hidden, such as the bookmark star, zoom, install app and file access.
Expired chrome://flags entries stay listed and usable, marked with a warning that they may stop working or disappear soon.
Groundwork so oganesson's own settings, text and preferences can plug into the browser; nothing visible on its own.
Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab show up under Next tab and Previous tab in the shortcut editor, with separate recently-used cycling commands when that mode is on.
New Scroll to top and Scroll to bottom commands that you can bind to a keyboard shortcut or mouse gesture.
Mouse gestures can run extensions' own commands, just as if their keyboard shortcut had been pressed.
The Shortcuts and gestures settings page lets you add, see, search and remove mouse gestures for every browser and extension command.
Hides the empty Passkeys entry in saved-info settings, since Linux has no passkey store without Google Password Manager.
Puts the "Passwords and autofill" submenu back in the three-dot menu, which Helium removes; oganesson keeps the password manager.
Right-button stroke, rocker and wheel mouse gestures work anywhere in the window, including internal pages, PDFs, tabs, toolbar and side panel.
Middle-clicking empty space on the horizontal tab strip opens a new tab, as in Firefox.
Middle-clicking empty space in the vertical tab strip opens a new tab, and clicks at the window edge reach the tabs.
Sign in with a Mozilla account, or point it at your own sync server, which works best. Passwords, bookmarks, history, open tabs, addresses and cards sync between oganesson, tennessine and Firefox.
The You and Sync settings page offers Firefox Sync sign-in and controls, and hides Google account and Google-only autofill sections.

No Helium servers: Helium's services, update checks, crash reports and onboarding are off, and so is fingerprint noise, which can be turned on. Chrome Web Store installs and updates and spellcheck dictionaries come from Google, as in Chromium, unless Browser traffic sends them through your own server.
The built-in uBlock Origin refreshes its filter list catalog from GitHub directly, so lists stay current with Helium's services off.
Firefox-style internal addresses such as about:addons, about:preferences, about:logins and about:support open the matching browser pages.
Release builds can target a newer x86-64 CPU level, such as x86-64-v2, for faster code on modern processors.
The built-in password manager offers to save passwords by default, and you can turn that off in settings.
Every toolbar item, including the address bar, buttons and pinned extensions, can be dragged anywhere and hidden, and the layout survives restarts.
Tab search sits on the toolbar instead of the tab strip, Chrome Labs is removed, and the Home button is shown or hidden from Customize toolbar.
Cycling tabs in recently-used order with Ctrl+Tab keeps working correctly when tabs are closed or moved during the cycle.
When recording a new keyboard shortcut, keys like Ctrl+T are captured instead of running, and Enter reliably saves the shortcut.
Installing and updating extensions from the Chrome Web Store reports the browser version, so the store serves compatible extension builds.
Installed web apps open outside links in your default browser, and each app gets editable scope rules, exclusions and a custom start address.

In an installed web app, a page that tries to move to an address outside the app, by script, form, redirect or history change, asks the browser first: the address opens in your default browser and the app page stays where it is. A "strict" option per app sends every page outside its scope out this way, popups included.
New tabs open and closing a tab selects the next one by Firefox's rules, for links, extensions and pinned tabs alike.
Reloading or updating an extension like uBlock Origin no longer leaves a page that was loading stuck blank.
An about:config page lists every browser preference and lets you edit it, like Firefox's about:config.
Makes menu item names visible to UI DevTools (a debugging tool) so automated tests can check menus; nothing visible on its own.
Switches to stop saving browsing history, download history and closed tabs (optionally kept in memory for the session); Firefox Sync then skips history too.
Privacy and security settings show the Don't save browsing history, Don't save download history and keep-closed-tabs switches.
Open tabs from your other Firefox Sync devices appear in History's Tabs from other devices and the app menu's Recent tabs.
Your Mozilla account's name and picture show on the profile button across restarts, which says Sync paused when you must sign in again.
Removes the media controls button that pops into the toolbar while media plays; Cast stays in the app menu.
Firefox-like address bar: choose and reorder suggestion sources, match bookmarks anywhere in title or address, and autofill sites from bookmarks and history.
An Address bar suggestions section in search engine settings with switches for history, bookmarks, open tabs and past searches, plus a suggestion order.
Firefox-style autoplay control: allow everything, block audio, or block audio and video until you click or type in the page itself.
Site settings get an Autoplay page with the three choices and per-site Allow or Block exceptions.
Tabs hide the sound-playing icon unless you turn it on, while muted, camera, microphone and screen-sharing icons always show.
Appearance settings get a Show sound icon on tabs switch.
On Wayland, dropping a link onto the split-view panel works even if the pointer stops moving before you release it.
Brands the browser as oganesson everywhere, with internal pages shown as oganesson:// while chrome:// still works.
On Linux the browser runs as oganesson, with its own desktop entry and its own profile in ~/.config/oganesson. A profile from the earlier "oganesson-focused" name is moved there once.
On Windows the browser installs and keeps its profile under %LOCALAPPDATA%\oganesson with its own file associations, URL scheme and policy key.
The Windows installer and zip ship the Firefox Sync library and the NSS files it needs, so Sync works on Windows.
Lets the Windows installer be packed on a Linux build machine, using its own copy of 7-Zip; nothing visible on its own.
Build fix for Windows: the installer's build waits for the V8 snapshot file it packs.

On Windows, a per-user install updates itself without prompts, with helium-windows' WinSparkle updater. It reads oganesson's own feed on dubna.zakius.xyz and installs an update only if its ed25519 signature matches the key built in. Updates are on by default, set by the Browser updates row in Settings > Browser traffic, and don't need Helium's services. All-users installs update by hand: their elevated updater needs an Authenticode signature, which the packages don't have.

As soon as an update is installed, by apt or dnf on Linux or the updater on Windows, the three-dot menu shows an "Update" chip and "Relaunch to update", which restarts into the new version with your windows, tabs and history kept.

Distrusts the six eMudhra TLS intermediates whose private keys leaked in October 2026, and Sectigo's cross-certificates of the same keys. Chrome blocks them through its downloaded revocation list, which oganesson doesn't fetch while component updates are off, so the block is built in.
On Linux the browser reads policies from /etc/oganesson/policies, not Chromium's /etc/chromium/policies, so policies written for Chromium don't apply to it.
t: Its own policy folder on Linux

w: Decides what the browser downloads by itself and which way each kind goes: certificate security data (CRLSet, the Chrome Root Store, the Certificate Transparency log list), Widevine, extensions, uBlock Origin's filter lists, spellcheck dictionaries, the !bang list and, on Windows, browser updates. Each goes direct to its source or through your own helium-services server, automatically or only when you ask, and never to Helium's own server. A row set to your server never falls back to a direct source. By default everything goes direct and stays current. Component update checks send no pings, and the app menu shows a badge when certificate data is more than a day old.

Settings > Privacy and security > Browser traffic replaces Helium's services page. Each kind of download has a row with Automatic or On request, and Direct or Proxy where both exist, under three presets: Direct (the default), Through my server and Shut in. One server field with a Test button and a health check serves every proxied row. When certificate data isn't automatic, a red warning says revoked certificates won't be blocked in time.

oganesson's own setup at chrome://settings/setup opens on a first start: Welcome, Import, Firefox Sync, Browser traffic, Search, Tabs, Passwords, Privacy extras, Default browser and Done. Every step but Welcome and Browser traffic can be skipped. A profile that had the browser before gets it once, with only the Browser traffic choice. Settings > About runs it again.
Built on Helium, carrying its whole patch series, including full uBlock Origin with Manifest V2 support built in.
Keeps useful features such as the password manager, Sync and Google search, but each is optional: DuckDuckGo is the default and Sync stays off until you sign in.
New profiles get one search engine list everywhere with DuckDuckGo first, the EU choice screen, and no search engine favicon fetching.
Signed apt and dnf repositories for Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora deliver updates with your normal system updates.
Runs on Linux x86-64 on X11 and Wayland; release builds target x86-64-v2 machines.
A Windows x64 build, cross-compiled on Linux, ships as an installer for one or all users and a portable zip.
Keeps its own profile, separate from Helium's and Chromium's.

Update policy: a new release in the current Chromium major version ships at once (as an experiment, the two browsers may differ within a major version). A new major version ships once Helium and Vanadium both have it. Fixes for exploits seen in the wild ship at once.
oganesson's own strings come with Polish translations.
Automated browser tests cover gestures, toolbar, tab behavior, web app links, autoplay, address bar suggestions and Sync before release.
Settings > Toolbar layout lets you reorder the toolbar's items, address bar included, and hide any except the address bar and menu.
Hide toolbar on scroll is a switch, off by default; when on, the toolbar hides as soon as a page loads, without Chromium's 3-second delay.
With the address bar at the bottom, the menu, search suggestions and tab switcher all run upward from it, the most-used item nearest your thumb.
The new tab page keeps the address bar where you put it, instead of moving it to the top, and drops its own search box.
Fixes a Chromium bug where, after swiping the toolbar between tabs, the toolbar stayed stuck on screen while the page scrolled under it.
The tab switcher is a compact vertical list (favicon, title, close button) instead of thumbnail cards; swipe-to-close, reordering and groups still work.
The address bar always shows the full URL, including https:// and www.
Page zoom follows Android's font size: a smaller system font makes whole pages smaller, multiplied with the default zoom setting.
The JavaScript JIT runs by default for speed; Vanadium's per-site setting stays, so you can still block it for any site.
On first run the browser downloads Helium's uBlock Origin build, checks it against a fixed SHA-256 checksum and installs it as an extension with Helium's extension ID, so its settings carry over.
The extensions puzzle button stays on the toolbar while no extension is pinned, so your extensions never end up out of reach.
A Firefox Sync account row sits at the top of Settings, like Firefox for Android, opening the Sync settings screen.
Ships Firefox Sync's Rust library (built for arm64) and its translated text in the APK; nothing visible on its own.
Privacy settings get switches to stop saving browsing history, closed tabs and download history, next to Close tabs on exit.
In installed web apps, a link's long-press menu opens it in your default browser, launched behind the web app; with tennessine as default, it becomes a background tab.
Settings > Autofill services names the built-in option "Autofill with Tennessine", using passwords, addresses and cards saved in the browser, Firefox Sync's included, not Google.
Settings > Last crash shows the stack trace of the last Java crash, so you can share it without adb.
Native libraries are stored compressed and the unused XR (headset/ARCore) module is dropped, so each download is about 190 MB instead of 340 MB. It takes about 110 MB more storage on the phone.
Vanadium's security hardening: safer compiler settings, memory tagging, W^X (memory can't be both writable and runnable), and strict site and origin isolation.
Vanadium keeps each site's stored data separate (state partitioning) and removes risky features, such as sensors, WebGPU and payments.
DuckDuckGo is the default search engine, with seven engines to choose from, Google among them.
A local password store that works without a Google account; Firefox Sync passwords build on it.
t: Password store without a Google account

w: Bookmark import and export, a barcode detector without Play services, and a WebRTC settings screen.
Off-by-default toggles to open external links and custom tabs in incognito, and a toggle to close tabs on exit.
Chrome extensions on a phone: a toolbar button, extension popups, and pinning extensions to the toolbar.
Manifest V2 extensions keep working.
Install extensions from the Chrome Web Store, Opera and Edge add-on sites, or unpacked from phone storage.
Extensions can run in incognito tabs.
DevTools on the phone.
Titanium's feature overrides, accessibility fixes, flags Chromium would have removed, and fixes for Chromium bugs.
n: automatic picture-in-picture stays off, as in Chromium: chrome://flags#auto-picture-in-picture-android turns it on

w: Search a specific site from the address bar; the address bar keeps its phone-style behavior.
Install from the project's F-Droid repository (https://packages.zakius.xyz/fdroid/repo) in F-Droid or Obtainium, with background updates.
The APK's native libraries are compressed with Zopfli before signing. F-Droid and Obtainium can't send only the changed parts of an update, so download size is what each update costs.

Among the Vanadium changes tennessine leaves out: HTTPS-Only mode as the default breaks sites with misconfigured redirects, so Chromium's quiet HTTPS upgrade with HTTP fallback stays. The built-in ad filter is left out because uBlock Origin does the blocking. GrapheneOS connectivity checks contact GrapheneOS servers, so Chromium's own Secure DNS is used.
One settings page with a separate, off-by-default switch for each Google-backed feature, each saying what it sends and to whom.
Lets autofill ask Google which form fields are which (crowdsourcing).
Page translation through Google, with the Translate settings and menu item back.
Chromium's translation that runs on your device. It downloads only the language packs.
Uses Google Cloud Messaging so sites can send you push messages while none of their tabs are open.
One switch for casting and for finding devices on your network (mDNS and DIAL).
A separate switch for each AI feature: Gemini in the browser, AI skills, AI permission prompts, page annotation models and Screen AI.
Tab-strip scrolling (off everywhere), close the window with the last tab, clear data on exit, close confirmation and a custom new tab page move from chrome://flags into Settings.
Passwords and autofill back in the app menu, the Password manager toolbar action, the "Manage passwords" footer on login forms, and password import if it works.
Settings > Behavior > Tab behavior: a Firefox (default) or Chromium preset over five rules for where new tabs open and which tab is selected after closing one, or any custom mix.
